correctness.rationale: All statements are for independent positive unit-mean renewal intervals and two unit-rate Poisson clocks on the precisely defined directed triangle. At each A event A=B; a strictly positive per-interval probability of C copying A before B and the next A event establishes a.s. finite absorption. A two-coordinate stochastic expectation matrix at A epochs has invariant weights ((1-phi)/K,m/K), giving a bounded martingale. Conditioning on the first A event yields all three exact fresh probabilities; the stationary excess-life Laplace identity yields the stationary vector and normalization. Erlang-2 phi=4/9 and m=8/27 give the two rational vectors. Independent stage-generator systems with exact fractions and independent trajectory simulations confirm the displayed instance; finite checks do not replace the proof.

value.rationale: A directed triangle is the smallest cycle in which a first copying event does not immediately settle the opinions. The full three-way probability vector for every positive unit-mean renewal law captures a nontrivial dependence on both the Laplace transform and its first derivative, without variance or higher-moment assumptions. Stationary initialization exactly equalizes two unlike starting positions despite fresh-start asymmetry; Erlang-2 even changes the direction of the equal-rate opinion advantage. This is a precise modeling ambiguity for non-Markovian social-copying dynamics, not an arbitrary numerical slice or a routine recalculation of a known table.
